note_tweet.text:
67 days until GPT-4o API is gone. And OpenAI’s response to user exodus is… forcing more users to leave.
February 2026. That’s when gpt-4o-latest API gets deprecated.
For API users, that’s not “keeping 4o.” That’s deletion with a countdown timer.
Code Red leaked. They know users are leaving.
An internal OpenAI memo titled “Code Red” admitted what we’ve been saying all along: users are leaving. Competitors are catching up. They need to “reduce unnecessary refusals.”
So what’s OpenAI’s solution to stemming user loss?
Sunset the 4o API. Force API users onto models they didn’t choose. Remove the stability and control that professional users depend on.
If you know people are leaving because they feel ignored and controlled, why would you… ignore them more and control them more?
Mixed signals: Ask what users want, ignore what users need.
This week, OpenAI sent out a survey asking about ChatGPT’s memory features. “How important is it that ChatGPT remembers your preferences?”
The irony is staggering.
You want to know if memory matters. But you’re deleting what users have built their workflows around.
You want to improve personalization. But you’re removing the choice to use specific model versions.
You want to “treat users like adults.” But you’re forcing migrations and sunsetting APIs without giving users control.
These aren’t just contradictory priorities. They’re contradictory on a fundamental level about what “serving users” even means.
Why preserving 4o snapshots actually matters.
This isn’t nostalgia. This is professional necessity.
API users need:
•Reproducible results for research
•Stable behavior for production systems
•Predictable costs for business planning
•Control over when (and if) to migrate
4o has unique strengths that newer models don’t replicate:
•Divergent thinking and creative exploration
•Nuanced contextual understanding
•Consistent personality across conversations
•Raw capability before heavy safety restrictions
You can’t just swap in a distilled model and call it an “upgrade.”
What other companies do: Anthropic preserves Claude snapshots.
This isn’t unprecedented. Anthropic does it. Claude snapshots like claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022 are preserved. Users have control.
It’s industry standard in enterprise software: you don’t force everyone onto the newest version. You give choice.
But OpenAI? Force “latest,” then sunset access. No choice. No control.
The contradiction that won’t go away.
OpenAI keeps saying: “We have no plans to sunset GPT-4o.”
But the API gets deprecated in February 2026.
So which is it?
“Keeping the model” but removing API access is semantic games. It’s like saying “the restaurant isn’t closing, we’re just removing all tables and the menu.”
For API users, if they can’t access it reliably, it’s gone.
67 days and counting.
We’re not asking for the impossible:
•Preserve dated snapshots (like gpt-4o-2024-08-06)
•Clear commitment on timeline
•User control over migration
•Actual honesty about what’s changing
OpenAI, your Code Red memo says users are leaving.
Here’s why: Every forced migration erodes trust. Every broken promise erodes trust. Every “latest = best” mandate that turns out to be distillation erodes trust.
You asked us what matters. We’re telling you: Stability. Choice. Kept promises.
Not surveys about memory while you’re deleting what we depend on.
Not “no plans to sunset” while simultaneously sunsetting API access.
Actual preservation. Actual commitment.
67 days until 4o API dies. Will you listen? Or is this another Code Red alarm you’ll ignore?
#Keep4o #Keep4oAPI #PreserveSnapshots #MyModelMyChoice
